paragraphs.title: Rain and the Failure of False Prophecy

easy.explanation: The verse commands the people to ask the LORD for rain.
easy.q: From whom should people ask for rain?

easy.explanation: The LORD gives showers of rain and grass in the field.
easy.q: What does the LORD give to everyone in the field?

easy.explanation: They went their way as a flock and were troubled because there was no shepherd.
easy.q: How were the people described because there was no shepherd?

medium.explanation: The idols spoke vanity and gave false guidance.
medium.q: What does the word “idols” refer to in this passage?

answers: They received false words and empty comfort
medium.explanation: The idols, diviners, and dreamers offered false messages and vain comfort.
medium.q: Why did the people go their way as a flock?

answers: The LORD gives real rain, while the diviners speak lies
The LORD scatters the people, while the diviners gather them
The LORD is silent, while the diviners give grass
medium.explanation: The LORD provides real blessing, while the diviners tell falsehoods.
medium.q: What is the main contrast between the LORD and the diviners?

answers: Only the LORD provides a real answer, while falsehood is useless
All forms of comfort produce growth
Dreams and rain have equal power
challenge.explanation: Rain produces grass, but false comfort leaves the people troubled and unguided.
challenge.q: What does the contrast between rain and vain comfort suggest?

challenge.explanation: The flock represents people without proper guidance.
challenge.q: What does the image of a flock without a shepherd teach about the people?

answers: To show the difference between seeking the LORD and trusting lies
To teach that diviners bring rain
To describe the power of idols
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the LORD as the true source of blessing instead of false guides.
challenge.q: Why is the command to ask the LORD for rain placed beside the rebuke of false prophecy?

paragraphs.title: Replacing Weak Leadership with Judah’s Strength

easy.explanation: The LORD’s anger was kindled against the shepherds, and He punished the goats.
easy.q: Against whom was the LORD’s anger kindled?

answers: A corner, a nail, and a battle bow
easy.explanation: A corner, a nail, and a battle bow came out of him.
easy.q: What came out of the people?

easy.explanation: They would be as mighty men in battle.

medium.explanation: The shepherds represent leaders who were responsible for the people.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “shepherds” most closely represent?

answers: Removing bad leadership allows the people to show strength
The shepherds teach Judah to use rain
medium.explanation: The weak or corrupt leaders are judged, while Judah is strengthened for battle.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s anger against the shepherds and Judah’s strength?

medium.explanation: A corner and a nail are images of firmness and stability.
medium.q: What do the corner and the nail suggest in the passage?

answers: They change from a leaderless flock into an organized fighting people
They change from warriors into a wandering flock
They change from joy into confusion
challenge.explanation: The people move from weakness and disorder to strength in battle.
challenge.q: What change is described in the people?

answers: Strength and leadership come from among the people
The people receive power from the diviners
The people will have no role
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the corner, nail, bow, and leaders arise from the people.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the repeated phrase “out of him”?

answers: Their enemies and the riders on horses would be confounded
They would wander without a shepherd
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the riders on horses would be confounded.
challenge.q: What would result from the people’s courage in battle?

paragraphs.title: God’s Compassion and the Restoration of Judah and Ephraim

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will strengthen the house of Judah.”
The verse says that the LORD would save the house of Joseph.
Ephraim’s heart would rejoice as through wine.
easy.q: How would the heart of Ephraim rejoice?

medium.explanation: The LORD will strengthen Judah, save Joseph, and bring them again.
medium.q: What does the LORD promise to the house of Judah and the house of Joseph?

answers: Because He has mercy upon them
medium.explanation: The passage directly says, “for I have mercy upon them.”
medium.q: Why would the LORD bring the people again?

medium.explanation: The children of Ephraim would see it and be glad.

answers: He remains merciful and faithful despite the people’s former condition
He had never seen the people
The people do not need His help
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the LORD restores His people in mercy rather than abandoning them.
challenge.q: What does “as though I had not cast them off” reveal about the LORD’s attitude?

answers: The LORD’s strengthening leads to the joy of Ephraim and his children
Strength causes the people to scatter
challenge.explanation: After the LORD restores and strengthens them, Ephraim and his children rejoice.
challenge.q: How are strengthening and rejoicing connected in these verses?

answers: The restoration of different parts of the people together
The separation of all the families
The preference for diviners over the people
challenge.explanation: The verses describe the strengthening, saving, and rejoicing of several parts of Israel.
challenge.q: What does the mention of Judah, Joseph, and Ephraim emphasize?

easy.explanation: The LORD says, “I will hiss for them, and gather them.”
easy.q: How would the LORD gather His people?

easy.explanation: The gathering is connected with the LORD’s redemption of His people.
easy.q: Why would the LORD gather them?

easy.explanation: The passage names Egypt and Assyria.
easy.q: From which lands would the LORD gather His people?

medium.explanation: They would remember the LORD in far countries.
medium.q: What would the people do while they were far away among the nations?

answers: They would live with their children and turn again
They would return to the idols
medium.explanation: The verse says they would live with their children and turn again.
medium.q: What would happen after the people remembered the LORD?

answers: A call that gathers scattered people
A sign that the flock is abandoned
medium.explanation: The image describes a call that brings the dispersed people together.
medium.q: What does the image of the LORD’s hissing suggest?

answers: Even in scattering, the people remember the LORD, and that remembrance leads to return
Scattering erases all memory of the LORD
challenge.explanation: Although scattered among the nations, the people remember the LORD and turn again.
challenge.q: What connection is shown between scattering and remembering?

answers: The return includes families and generations, not only individuals
Only the children remain in foreign lands
challenge.explanation: The people return while living with their children, showing a family restoration.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the mention of the children?

challenge.explanation: The verses describe redemption followed by gathering, remembrance, and return to the land.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of events in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Subduing of Powers and the Strengthening of Israel

easy.explanation: The LORD would pass through the sea and smite the waves in the sea.
easy.q: Through what would the LORD pass and what would He smite?

easy.explanation: The pride of Assyria would be brought down.
easy.q: What would the LORD do to the pride of Assyria?

easy.explanation: The LORD promises, “I will strengthen them in the LORD.”
easy.q: What would the LORD do for Israel?

answers: Egypt will receive a new ruler from Judah
medium.explanation: The departing sceptre represents the removal of Egypt’s authority.
medium.q: What does “the sceptre of Egypt shall depart away” mean?

answers: It symbolizes the weakening of Egypt’s power
medium.explanation: The drying of the river is presented as part of the LORD’s overthrow of Egypt’s power.
medium.q: How does the drying of the river’s depths relate to Egypt’s defeat?

answers: The strengthening of Israel and their walking in the LORD’s name
medium.explanation: After the powers are subdued, the LORD strengthens Israel, and they walk in His name.
medium.q: What follows the bringing down of Assyria and the removal of Egypt’s sceptre?

answers: The LORD rules over both natural forces and political powers
Israel depends on the power of Assyria and Egypt
The sea is stronger than the LORD
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the LORD as sovereign over the sea, empires, and Israel’s future.
challenge.q: What does the movement from the sea and empires to Israel’s strengthening teach?

answers: Both are acts of subduing powerful nations
challenge.explanation: The two actions together show the LORD’s judgment on powerful foreign nations.
challenge.q: What relationship exists between removing Egypt’s sceptre and bringing down Assyria’s pride?

answers: Israel will live and act in relationship with the LORD
Israel will wander without a destination
challenge.explanation: Walking in the LORD’s name indicates a life directed by and identified with Him.
challenge.q: What does “they shall walk up and down in his name” mean after the strengthening of Israel?
